title: Dynamics
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Dynamics Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: Apply the relationship between resultant force, mass and acceleration (F = ma) to new situations; identify the forces acting on an object and draw free-body diagrams; explain the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces and of friction; state that mass is a measure of the amount of matter and of inertia, that weight is a gravitational force and that gravitational field strength is the force per unit mass (W = mg, g = 10 N/kg) (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on dynamics: balanced and unbalanced forces, free-body diagrams, F = ma, friction, mass, weight (W = mg) and inertia. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

An unbalanced (resultant) force makes an object accelerate.

  • Balanced forces: the object stays at rest or keeps moving at constant velocity.
  • F = ma, where F is the resultant force in N, m in kg and a in m/s². Find the resultant first (forward forces − backward forces).
  • Friction opposes motion. Weight W = mg (g = 10 N/kg) is a force in N; mass in kg is the same everywhere and measures inertia.
Example

A 1200 kg car: driving force 3000 N, friction 600 N. Acceleration?

resultant = 3000 − 600 = 2400 N

a = 2400 ÷ 1200

Answer: 2 m/s²

Example

Weight of a 55 kg student?

W = 55 × 10

Answer: 550 N

Common mistakes

  • Using the driving force in F = ma instead of the resultant force.
  • Giving weight in kg. Weight is a force, in newtons.
  • Thinking a moving object needs a resultant force to keep moving. At constant velocity the resultant force is zero.
  • Thinking mass changes on the Moon. Only weight changes.

faq.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
faq.a: Mass is the amount of matter in a body (kg) and does not change; weight is the gravitational force on it (N), W = mg.

faq.q: What happens when the forces on an object are balanced?
faq.a: The resultant force is zero, so the object stays at rest or moves at a constant velocity.

faq.q: How do you use F = ma with friction?
faq.a: Subtract the friction (and other resistive forces) from the driving force to get the resultant force, then divide by the mass.

items.q: Zhi Hao and a friend push a stalled car in the same direction with 145 N and 45 N. What is the resultant force (ignore friction)?
items.e: Same direction: add. 145 + 45 = 190 N.

items.q: A cyclist speeds up along a flat road. Which statement is correct?
c: The forces are unbalanced: the resultant force acts forwards.
There are no forces acting on it.
The forces are unbalanced: the resultant force acts downwards.
The forces are balanced: the resultant force is zero.
items.e: Balanced forces: constant velocity (or at rest). Unbalanced forces: acceleration in the direction of the resultant force.

items.q: In a tug-of-war, the left team pulls with 70 N and the right team pulls with 25 N. What is the resultant force?
items.e: Opposite directions: subtract; the larger force wins.

items.q: In which direction does friction act on a box sliding to the right?
items.e: Friction opposes motion.

items.q: A car moves along a straight road at a constant speed. Which statement is correct?
c: There are no forces acting on it.
The forces are unbalanced: the resultant force acts downwards.
The forces are unbalanced: the resultant force acts forwards.
The forces are balanced: the resultant force is zero.
items.e: Balanced forces: constant velocity (or at rest). Unbalanced forces: acceleration in the direction of the resultant force.

items.q: In a tug-of-war, the left team pulls with 115 N and the right team pulls with 65 N. What is the resultant force?
items.e: Opposite directions: subtract; the larger force wins.

items.q: What is meant by gravitational field strength?
c: the gravitational force per unit mass
items.e: g = W ÷ m.

items.q: A trolley is pushed with 10 N to the right and 30 N to the left. What is the resultant force?
items.e: Opposite forces subtract: 30 − 10 = 20 N, towards the bigger force.

items.q: Why is it harder to push a loaded trolley than an empty one?
c: It has more mass, so more inertia.
items.e: More mass means more force is needed for the same acceleration.

items.q: What is inertia?
c: the force that stops moving objects
the reluctance of a body to change its state of rest or motion
items.e: Mass is a measure of inertia.

items.q: In a tug-of-war, the left team pulls with 120 N and the right team pulls with 65 N. What is the resultant force?

items.q: What does a free-body diagram show?

the forces the object exerts on others
items.e: Arrow length shows the size of each force.

items.q: Two people push a toy car to the right with forces of 18 N and 30 N. What is the resultant force?
items.e: Forces in the same direction add: 18 + 30 = 48 N.

items.q: A skydiver falls at terminal velocity. Which statement is correct?
c: The forces are balanced: the resultant force is zero.
The forces are unbalanced: the resultant force acts forwards.
There are no forces acting on it.

items.e: Balanced forces: constant velocity (or at rest). Unbalanced forces: acceleration in the direction of the resultant force.

items.q: Two forces act on a crate: 30 N to the right and 30 N to the left. What happens if it is at rest?
items.e: Balanced forces give zero resultant force.

items.q: A crate is pushed with 30 N to the right and 22 N to the left. What is the resultant force?
items.e: Opposite forces subtract: 30 − 22 = 8 N, towards the bigger force.

items.q: A crate is pushed with 32 N to the right and 28 N to the left. What is the resultant force?
items.e: Opposite forces subtract: 32 − 28 = 4 N, towards the bigger force.

items.q: A car brakes and slows down. Which statement is correct?
c: The forces are unbalanced: the resultant force acts forwards.
There are no forces acting on it.
The forces are balanced: the resultant force is zero and it stays at rest.
The forces are unbalanced: the resultant force acts backwards.
items.e: Balanced forces: constant velocity (or at rest). Unbalanced forces: acceleration in the direction of the resultant force.

items.q: A trolley is pushed with 34 N to the right and 40 N to the left. What is the resultant force?
items.e: Opposite forces subtract: 40 − 34 = 6 N, towards the bigger force.
